si_4_title: Lifespan Normative Models of White Matter Fractional Anisotropy: Applications to Early Psychosis
sc_1_study_objective: To develop large-scale normative models of Fractional Anisotropy (FA) across the lifespan and apply them to an early psychosis cohort to investigate white matter alterations and their relationship with clinical symptoms.

caa_7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of mean deviations (t-test with FDR correction) and proportions of extreme deviations (Mann-Whitney U test with FDR correction). A multi-view sparse canonical correlation analysis (msCCA) with stability selection was used to find associations between multimodal (FA, cortical thickness, subcortical volume) brain deviations and symptom domains (PANSS).
caa_8_key_findings_brief: Normative models revealed significant inter-individual heterogeneity in white matter structure in early psychosis, and a multimodal analysis linked these deviations in the right uncinate fasciculus and thalamus to cognitive symptom severity.
caa_9_key_findings_detailed: While no significant group differences in mean FA deviations were found after FDR correction, individuals with psychosis showed a significantly greater proportion of extreme positive and negative Z-scores compared to controls (p<0.004). A multivariate msCCA analysis combining FA and structural deviations identified a significant association with clinical symptoms (mean test canonical correlation r=0.25, p=0.003), driven primarily by the cognitive factor and total PANSS scores. Stability selection revealed that FA in the right uncinate fasciculus and bilateral thalamus volume were the most robust predictors of symptom severity.

caa_10_key_limitations.answer: The age distribution of the reference dataset is skewed, with fewer participants at the extremes of the lifespan (ages 5-8 and >85). The models do not account for all demographic factors like socioeconomic background. The reference dataset is biased towards 'Western Educated, Industrialised, Rich and Democratic' (WEIRD) populations, and self-reported race is an imperfect proxy for ethnicity.
caa_10_key_limitations.supporting_text: The age distribution in our dataset is skewed, with fewer data points at the extremes of the lifespan particularly in young children between the ages of 5 and 8 and adults over 85 years old...Additionally, while our models effectively account for site-specific differences, variability due to demographic factors like socioeconomic background was not fully explored...it should be remembered that the datasets on which these models were trained on are not representative of the wider population and are themselves biased towards 'Western Educated, Industrialised, Rich and Democratic' (WEIRD) populations [40]. Self-reported race is also an imperfect proxy for ethnicity...

caa_11_application_notes: The study demonstrates a multimodal data fusion approach by combining FA deviations with cortical thickness and subcortical volume deviations to predict clinical symptoms. It also uses transfer learning to apply the large-scale normative model to a new clinical dataset with a small amount of local control data for calibration.
gn_1_general_note: The study provides the trained normative models for public use through an open-source software platform (PCNtoolkit) and GitHub. The models were created for Fractional Anisotropy (FA), but the authors plan to extend them to other diffusion metrics like MD and NODDI. Two versions of the models are released: one that accounts for self-reported race and one that does not, allowing researchers to choose the most appropriate model for their data.
